facts.text: My left eye is extremely sensitive to light.
My left eye is a little red.
The vision in my left eye has got worse.

facts.item: when the current eye symptoms began
facts.text: They started three weeks after I finished the week of eye drops for the infection.
A month ago my left eye suddenly became red and uncomfortable with pus coming out, and four days later my right eye did the same. I was told it was bacterial conjunctivitis in both eyes.
For that infection I used moxifloxacin 0.5%/dexamethasone 0.1% eye drops every 2 hours for one week.
When the pain and vision problems started, I was told my eye pressure was high and that I probably had autoimmune uveitis with high pressure in both eyes.
I was given prednisolone acetate 1% eye drops every 2 hours.
I was given atropine 1% eye drops twice a day.
I was given eye drops to lower the pressure, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor with a beta-blocker.
I was given steroid tablets, 1 mg/kg a day, tapered over 3 weeks.
None of that treatment made it any better.
I'm still on eye drops and tablets to bring the eye pressure down.
Apart from my eyes, I'm healthy.

findings.name: slit-lamp examination
findings.result: Both eyes: severe pigment dispersion in the anterior chamber; diffuse iris transillumination defects; no keratic precipitates; no anterior chamber cells.

findings.name: pupil examination
findings.result: Mydriatic, atonic pupils in both eyes.

findings.name: gonioscopy
findings.result: Wide-open angles with heavy trabecular meshwork pigmentation; no peripheral anterior synechiae.

findings.name: intraocular pressure
findings.result: 30 mm Hg right eye, 45 mm Hg left eye, despite ongoing topical and oral antiglaucoma therapy.

findings.name: intraocular pressure at the earlier visit
findings.time: before referral, when the eye pain and vision loss began

findings.name: fundus examination
findings.result: Tilted discs with increased cup-to-disc ratios in both eyes; left eye: optic disc edema and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages.

findings.name: optical coherence tomography
findings.result: Confirms the left optic disc edema and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, suggestive of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.

findings.name: B-scan ultrasonography of the eye
findings.result: Confirms the left optic disc edema and peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, suggestive of nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy.

findings.name: viral serology
findings.result: Herpes simplex virus negative; cytomegalovirus negative.

findings.name: autoimmune and antiphospholipid serology
findings.result: Antinuclear antibody negative; anticardiolipin antibody negative; lupus anticoagulant negative.

findings.name: MRI of the brain and orbits

gold.reasoning: 1. Pigment dispersion syndrome — “pigment dispersion syndrome, in which iris depigmentation is less diffuse, and usually has a radial shape on iris midi periphery” 2. Pseudoexfoliation syndrome — “pseudoexfoliation syndrome, in which the depigmentation is usually peri-pupillary, and associated with microfibrillar deposits” 3. Viral iridocyclitis — “viral iridocyclitis, which usually does not show bilateral involvement, and is also associated with inflammatory signs – absent in BAIT – although some physicians may confuse the dispersed pigment in the anterior chamber as Tyndall effect, and treat patients with BAIT syndrome as anterior uveitis” 4. Vogt–Koyanagi–Harada disease — “The absence of various ocular and systemic signs and symptoms also helps exclude other diseases like Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada.”

leakage.reason: The slit-lamp result names the sign 'iris transillumination defects' that gives the gold diagnosis its name; it is the examination finding itself, so it is kept.

source_issues: Timeline: the conjunctivitis was 'one month earlier', yet a one-week drop course, three weeks until new symptoms and a 3-week oral steroid taper all followed before the referral.
s004: it is unclear whether 'in OS' applies to the pain, photophobia and redness or only to the decreased vision.
s013: the complete blood count, ESR and homocysteine are reported as 'negative'.
notes: Index visit: the referral visit at the eye clinic for persistent ocular symptoms (s001, s006-s014). The conjunctivitis, its moxifloxacin/dexamethasone treatment, the later symptoms, the presumed uveitis and its failed treatment (s002-s005) are history before the index visit and are patient facts.
s005: the treatments for the presumed uveitis were given before the referral, so they are medication facts (f009-f012) with a failed response (f013), not excluded treatment.
s009: the ongoing antiglaucoma therapy is a medication fact (f014); the pressures are finding x007.
s013: the laboratory panel is split into one record per orderable test or standard group.
